content: The postglacial cap carbonate layer is situated above the Chuos diamictite. Beneath the Chuos glaciation lies the Naauwpoort Formation, which has been radiometrically dated to 746 ± 2 million years ago (Ma), providing an upper age limit for the base of the Chuos Formation. Modern stratigraphic analyses conducted several hundred kilometers west of the Otavi Mountain Land reveal that the Chuos Formation is embedded within a rift-related, fault-bounded paleotopography. This structural setting causes the substrate of the Chuos Formation to vary along its strike, particularly across the southern flank of the Owambo Basin. In the region encompassing the Ghaub and Varianto farms, the stratigraphic sequence includes the Nabis Sandstone Formation of the Nosib Group, which is overlain by the Chuos Formation and subsequently succeeded by the Berg Aukas Formation. This area has been mapped at a scale of 1:250,000 by the Geological Survey of Namibia. The Beiyixi glaciation occurred after 755 Ma. The Kundelungu Formation has been dated to 765 ± 5 Ma. The Sinian period spans approximately 800 to 542 Ma. The Hadrynian period, as defined in North America, spans 850 to 542 Ma. The Namibian period, defined in South Africa, spans 900 to 542 Ma. The Mesoproterozoic era, a geologic time frame within the Proterozoic eon, encompasses the Calymmian, Ectasian, and Stenian periods, ranging from approximately 1600 to 900 million years ago. This era is notable for the formation of the Rodinia supercontinent. The Tonian period spans 1000 to 850 Ma and is significant for the emergence of the first putative metazoan (animal) fossils, such as Otavia antiqua, which has been described as a sponge. The dating of these fossils aligns with molecular data obtained from genetic studies of modern metazoan species, suggesting that the base of the animal phylogenetic tree lies within the Tonian period. The Karatau period spans 1100 to 800 Ma. The Stenian period, the final geologic period of the Mesoproterozoic era, spans 1200 to 1000 Ma. The Adelaidean period, defined in Australia, spans 1300 to 542 Ma. The Ectasian period, within the Mesoproterozoic era, spans 1400 to 1200 Ma. The Calymmian period, also within the Mesoproterozoic era, spans 1600 to 1400 Ma. The Helikian period, defined in North America, spans 1600 to 850 Ma. The Paleoproterozoic era, another geologic era within the Proterozoic eon, spans 2500 to 1600 Ma. This era is characterized by the proliferation of cyanobacteria, which significantly increased atmospheric oxygen levels, fundamentally altering life on Earth. The Jinningian period, defined in China, spans 1750 to 800 Ma. The Carpentarian period spans 1800 to 1300 Ma. The Kombolgie Formation of the MacArthur Basin in the Northern Territory, dated to approximately 1400 to 1500 Ma, overlies or has overlain unconformity-type uranium deposits. A study of clay minerals isolated from carbonate rocks of the McMinn Formation provides an isochron age of 1429 ± 31 Ma, marking the cessation of sedimentation in the Proterozoic McArthur Basin.
